text:
john_customer: Hey team — since the last rollout our integration is returning different policy text for identical prompts in the same session. Very inconsistent, customer is losing trust.

elena_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste one request/response with X-Request-ID and session id?

john_customer: sure. session=acct-92: here are two back-to-back calls, same prompt. Note different model text.
```
> curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/completions \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "X-Request-ID: r-9a3f" \n  -d '{"session_id":"acct-92","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is our refund policy for subscription cancellations?"}]}'

200 OK
{ "model":"redwood-chat-xl-v2", "choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"Refunds are processed within 5 business days. We do not refund prorated months."}}]}

--- second call ---
X-Request-ID: r-9a4g
{ "model":"redwood-chat-xl-v2-quant", "choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"Customers are refunded immediately upon approval, pro-rated refunds may apply."}}]}
```

elena_support: Hmm different wording and semantics — both show xl variant names but flavors differ. Could be fallback/routing mixing? tagging @raj_engineer and @sam_oncall.

raj_engineer: Thanks — visible mismatch between final lines. Do you have correlation ids from our router (route-id header) or the full request log? Also was this during a rollout window?

john_customer: route-id header: route=eu-west-1:pool-b. Rollout started ~2026-03-10 02:00 UTC. Happened repeatedly today.

marta_product: We did a canary last week that introduced an optimized quantized variant (xl-v2-quant) for cheaper tokens. There was supposed to be sticky routing per session. Possibly sticky hash key not applied.

sam_oncall: Quick check of logs for acct-92: I see alternating invocations to xl-v2 and xl-v2-quant for same session hash within ~10s window. Looks like session affinity failing when autoscaler spawns a new pod.

raj_engineer: That matches hypothesis. When affinity lost, router picks cheapest compatible variant in target pool — quant variant has slightly different decoding defaults -> semantic shift.

elena_support: Customer is requesting rollback to previous stable behavior until we fix. Can we do a targeted rollback for acct-92 or enforce session affinity?

marta_product: We can add a per-tenant override to prefer non-quantized variants, but that's a config change and needs auth. For immediate relief we can pin acct-92 to dedicated pool (manual route) or create a routing rule that matches session id prefix.

raj_engineer: For immediate mitigation: I can push a routing rule: match header X-Tenant-ID: acct-92 -> prefer pool-b:xl-v2 (non-quant). Will need deploy-bot confirmation and a short cache flush.

deploy_bot: config-change requested by raj_engineer: apply routing rule 'tenant:acct-92 prefer:xl-v2' -> pending review.

sam_oncall: After applying rule we should also monitor KV cache hits; if new pod caused cache miss, prompts could still generate different completions due to changed key-prefix. Patch in-flight to ensure KV cache migrates on pod spawn.

raj_engineer: Applied rule and flushed router cache (rule id r-acct92-001). Please repro.

john_customer: testing now — sending same prompt twice.

john_customer: both responses now match, consistent. Thanks.

elena_support: Great. I'll note mitigation and escalate for permanent fix. Steps: 1) Temporary tenant routing rule (done). 2) Fix session-affinity logic on autoscaler/pool spawn. 3) Add explicit compatibility tag for variants to avoid semantic jumps. 4) Postmortem and customer communication.

marta_product: I'll schedule postmortem and soak test with canary traffic. We'll also offer the customer a small credit for trouble.

raj_engineer: Action items for eng: reproduce locally with autoscaler simulation, write a unit test for affinity hash persistence, add e2e test that compares outputs between variant families.

elena_support: I'll follow up with customer tomorrow with status + credit. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
